title: Japanese City Ends Traditional School Club System
paragraphs: The city of Kobe in western Japan has ended its traditional school club system for public middle schools. Instead, students can now join activities run by local community groups.

In Japan, school clubs, known as "bukatsu," have long been an important part of student life. Many students join sports teams, music groups or art clubs after school, and teachers usually lead these activities.

However, as of September 1, 2026, 82 public middle schools in Kobe have completely ended their club activities. These include sports teams, brass bands and art clubs. The decision was recommended by the Kobe Board of Education, and it is permanent.

There are two main reasons for the change. First, teachers in Japan are very busy. They have to prepare lessons and also coach or advise clubs, which makes their working hours very long. Second, because of Japan's falling birthrate, there are fewer students. Many clubs did not have enough members, and some schools had already closed some of their teams.

To replace the school clubs, the city started a new program called "Kobekatsu" on the same day. It works with 1,051 local sports teams, clubs, workshops and universities. They offer activities in sports, the arts and technology.

Joining these activities costs money. On average, students pay 3,200 yen a month. To help families, the city gives students between 1,500 and 3,000 yen a month. There is also a fund to help pay for equipment, such as sports goods and musical instruments.

The new system has some possible advantages. Students can choose from many more activities, and they can meet students from other schools. But some people worry that students may feel less pride in their school, because their teams will no longer represent it.
